Avant-corps.subject: Important Days
Avant-corps.question: The _____ was Protruding part of a building.
Avant-corps.fact: An avant-corps (Italian: avancorpo or risalto, plural risalti, German: Risalit, Polish: ryzalit), a French term literally meaning "fore-body", is a part of a building, such as a porch or pavilion, that juts out from the corps de logis, often taller than other parts of the building.

Avant-corps.subject: Important Days
Avant-corps.question: It is common in façades in _____ architecture
Avant-corps.fact: It is common in façades in French Baroque architecture.

Avant-corps.subject: Important Days
Avant-corps.question: Particularly in _____ architecture, a corner Risalit is where two wings meet at right angles
Avant-corps.fact: An avant-corps (Italian: avancorpo or risalto, plural risalti, German: Risalit, Polish: ryzalit), a French term literally meaning "fore-body", is a part of a building, such as a porch or pavilion, that juts out from the corps de logis, often taller than other parts of the building. Particularly in German architecture, a corner Risalit is where two wings meet at right angles.
